Read out of saint.gr's line for 7 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Νείλος εκ Ρωσίας», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 7 April on pravoslavno.rs, „Преп. Нил Сорски.“, with the rank word Преп. left off. The by-name Сорски is kept, because it is what the heading gives beyond the forename and what distinguishes him from the seven other folders of the name.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 7 mai — «Sfântul Nil Sorski»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Νείλος εκ Ρωσίας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους» and «(1433 - 1508)», and names him in its first words, «Ο Όσιος Νείλος του Σόρκιυ» — Nilus of Sora, of the noble family of the Maikovs. That is this folder's man. **`dates` are not touched**: the folder already holds 1433 and 1508 and the Greek agrees on both. **The Greek's own day for his repose is a moveable one**: «κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη την Κυριακή των Μυροφόρων του 1508 μ.Χ.», the Sunday of the Myrrhbearers, which no fixed feast can hold; the calendar keeps him on this fixed 7 May and the moveable Sunday is recorded here and in the report, not forced into a day. **What the Greek adds**: the birth at Moscow of devout parents, the work as a shorthand writer in the service of the great prince of Moscow, the monastery of the White Lake founded by the ascetic Cyril, the journey to the Holy Mountain with his fellow monk Innocent and the ascetic life in the Skete of the Carpenter, the report that he stayed a long while at the monastery of Saint Dionysius, the return to Russia about 1480, the hermitage on the river Sora and the little church of the Meeting of the Lord he built there, his measure and discretion and his willingness to be taken for a fool in order to be useful to the brethren, his part against the Judaizers of Novgorod who set the end of the world at the year 7000 from the creation, that is 1492, the question of monastic property he raised at the Moscow council of 1503 which the council did not adopt, and the ascetic writings. No Greek hymn is printed.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 20.04.2026 (7. април ст. ст.) — „Преп. Нил Сорски.“

attestations.note: The day's second entry, and **the Prologue keeps him on a day neither other calendar keeps him on**: doxologia.ro and saint.gr both have him on 7 May, and this is the Julian 7 April, a month off and not a style conversion. One row per church is the schema, so the Serbian row carries the Prologue's own day, nothing was moved and nothing was displaced; the divergence is recorded here and in the life rather than reconciled. The man is the same beyond doubt — Nilus of Sora, one of the great fathers of the Russian church, the founder of the skete life of monks in Russia, reposed 1508 — and the 1508 agrees exactly with the `attested` 1508 this folder holds off doxologia's own «La 7 mai 1508 și-a dat sufletul său în mâinile lui Hristos», so **no date was touched**. New to the folder, and all of it in four sentences: that the Prologue calls him **one of the great fathers of the Russian church** and **the founder of the skete monastic life in Russia**; that **his relics rest in the Sora monastery** — worth noting beside the testament this folder already records, in which he asked that his body be thrown into a waste place for the beasts and the birds, since no source read before this one said where the relics are; and that his **Устав скитског живота, his Rule of the skete life, is a spiritual and practical work of the first order**. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion, and this folder has no hymn from any source.
